newsitem.title: CANADA: TENNIS-CALLENS IS SURPRISE FINALIST IN QUEBEC.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CALLENS IS SURPRISE FINALIST IN QUEBEC.

text.p: Little-known Els Callens of Belgium picked off her third successive seeded player on Saturday to advance to the final of the Bell Challenge tennis tournament against fifth-seeded American Lisa Raymond.
The 73-ranked Callens opened her semifinal with "the best set of my life" to surprise second seed Elena Likhovtseva of Russia 6-0 6-4.
Callens will get her chance to make it four seeds in a row Sunday when she faces the 44th-ranked Raymond, a 6-3 6-4 victor over unseeded compatriot Tami Whitlinger-Jones.
Callens beat Raymond on grass in Birmingham, England last June in their only previous meeting. Both will be going for her first career title on the WTA Tour Sunday.
The 26-year-old from Antwerp had already upset third seed Amy Frazier and sixth-seeded Argentine Florencia Labat before blitzing the 24th-ranked Likhovtseva in the first set.
"I didn't expect her to start that good," admitted Likhovtseva.
Despite a closer score, Raymond, a two-time U.S. collegiate champion, overpowered the 80th-ranked Whitlinger-Jones. She took at 3-0 lead in the opening set and was always in control.
"When I was aggressive and attacking, I won most of the points," Raymond said. "My ground strokes were really good and I didn't need to come in to the net more."

The lanky Callens, who seemed to come from out of nowhere this week, displayed a powerful serve and flat, penetrating groundstrokes, which she used to keep Likhovtseva off balance on the fast indoor court.
She later explained that she got a late start on her professional tennis career and hoped to make up for lost time.
"I didn't start the tour until I was 20 and finished school," she explained.
"I only practiced three hours a week in school and then I started out at the lowest tournaments. I didn't get wild cards like Jennifer Capriati and Martina Hingis."
Another win on Sunday and the wild card may start coming for Callens.
